Notes to Authors

It the policy of this Journal to publish articles in English in all fields of ISLAM provided they are of a high caliber and contribute to the fundamental knowledge of the religion. In keeping with the universal nature of Islam, this journal is not intended to reflect any political, regional, or nationalistic bias. Articles containing unwarranted attacks, direct or implied, against any other religion, sect, belief, or ideology, shall not be accepted for publication. The journal's sole objective is to work within the framework of ISLAM towards a full appreciation of God's message to all humanity.

The journal recognizes the sources of Islamic knowledge to be the Qur'an, the Sunna, analogy (Qiyas), consensus (Ijma'), and personal thought (Ijtihad). However, THE QUR'AN shall be the ultimate reference. Only statements in full agreement with the Qur'an shall represent the journal's official stand. All other statements, or statements subject to various interpretations shall represent only the author's personal viewpoint.

Manuscripts submitted for publication should be typed, double spaced. Only one copy is required. All Qur'anic quotations must be accompanied by the number(s) of sura(s), and the number(s) of verse(s). Colons should separate the number of sura from the number(s) of verse(s) (e.g. 17:28-33). A group of verses from the same sura should be separated from each other by commas (e.g. 17:28-33, 51, 60-62). When more than one sura are involved, a semi-colon should separate the different suras (e.g. 17:28-33, 51, 60-62; 23:16; 36:9-11, 19-25, 44). The journal will undertake to add the Arabic text to all Qur'anic translations. This is to avoid the inadvertent mental re-translation to an Arabic composition which is different from the original.

Every Hadith should be accompanied by its sources (transmitters) and the reference book where it may be found. If the transmitter(s) and/or the reference book were not known, this should be stated clearly.

ISLAM: Its Mission in the World
2. CONDEMNATION OF THE PRINCIPLE OF BLIND IMITATION
by Professor M. Farid Wajdi

Of all his achievements as writer, editor of Nour-el-Islam, and Professor at Al-Azhar University, Dr. Wajdi is better known for his famous Qur'anic commentary. This series of articles, which were written by him in Arabic, promises to be a most cherished feature by ALL readers of Islam.

In all ages throughout the human history, reformers were never confronted with a stronger obstacle than that of blind imitation of forefathers and leaders of old religions. This inaction has been the cause of the persistence to this day of corrupted religions whose survival in our times is a slur on the human intellect. It was equally responsible for the continual existence of certain sects which exploited the ignorance of people who were otherwise well-fitted to take their place among the rising nations but have for this reason remained in stygian darkness down to the present day.

Only one who has made a thorough study of the religions professed by the majority of contemporary nations as well as of the few hundred minor divisions derived therefrom, could appreciate the pernicious influence exercised by blind imitation over the life of people and the harm involved in the consequent antagonism to learning and reason. Next to the establishment of its principal beliefs, Islam has striven against the tendency of blind imitation into which people have long lapsed without having it examined or assayed by reason.

Indeed, this rational idea could never have been conceived by minds in those dark and remote times when humanity was yet under age. But when humanity attained maturity in the generations that followed, this idea became an essential element of the universal religion which was ordained by the Lord in His last dispensation, not only to conform with the momentous intellectual development that took place, but also to rouse the religious sentiment in the hearts of men and inspire them to still greater and higher attainments.

Those interested in the investigation of human affairs of recent times will find out that souls have discarded all moral restraints and have fallen an easy prey to unbridled passion and wickedness while the religious sentiment

ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(2): 85-90

ISLAM: ITS MISSION IN THE WORLD

which constitutes the supreme moral power mitigating those excesses, has become incapable to discharge its function in many a nation. It was on account of this that other agents were sought to counteract those excesses. Some have sought such agents in science, in the power of public opinion or in some human instinct. But the investigator who goes deeply into the initial causes of things, will soon realize that, of all human instincts, the religious sentiment is best suited to counteract those excesses and to wield the most beneficial influence over the souls of men. If, however, it has become unequal to the task in certain nations, it is only on account of the weakness which affected their religions and which was the outcome of what was impressed on the people as being traditional matters to be followed or disregarded as a whole. But if they knew that a religion existed which severely censures imitation and imitators, and insists on reasoning and consideration, a religion whose beliefs are founded on evidence and truth, and is withal framed in a system which surpasses that of modern scientific investigation in reasoning and accuracy, their hopes in regaining the influence of religion will be roused again. For once this influence is regained the religious sentiment is awakened and its power will once more be felt in the guidance of men and in setting up a virtuous civilization for the world.

It was for this reason that Islam has striven hard to overcome the obstacle of blind imitation and has attempted to do this by different ways of reasoning aiming thereby at three objects:
1. To spread its life-giving principles calculated to revive humanity in its later days.
2. To conserve for the religious sentiment its intrinsic power which enables it to restrain the human passions and safeguard the people from being carried away by wickedness.
3. To render the system of religious investigation more advanced and more accurate than that of scientific investigation so that the latter may not overwhelm the former and put it into insignificance.

This is a great objective at which Islam aimed so that reason may not hold undisputed sway over souls independent of the religious sentiment which the Lord has set to mitigate the brutal tendencies attendant on the human state and which no intellectual culture could restrain.

This could only come about by convincing reason, by proof, to give due regard to that sentiment and to admit the power exercised by it. Thus, reason will not concede unless that sentiment is established on a like system of research and investigation and is equally free of any traces of imitation unsupported by material or mental evidence.

ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(2)

M. Farid Wajdi

By so doing, Islam has succeeded to associate reason with the religious sentiment for the first time in the history of religions. It has succeeded, on the strength of these two great principles, to raise a nation which attained to the height of human progress and took the lead in both moral and scientific culture as well as in the religious leadership of the world. Islam was thus rendered equal to establish the highest civilization on earth without the conflict between religion and reason and without people degenerating in their morals and propensities as is the case in the present day civilization.

Let us now consider how far has Islam succeeded to fulfill this great project.

Islam was revealed at a time when people were the slaves of false and corrupted religions which they inherited from their forefathers and from which they could not be moved. Any one who wished to move them therefrom was regarded by them as a bitter enemy merely because he attempted to bring about a reform.

The campaign was first opened by admonitions and threats thus awakening in men the instinct of reasoning and urging them to reflection and consideration of the sad end to which past nations have come. This done, Islam began to attack the main cause which prevented them to consider any reform viz. the blind imitation of their forefathers even though they were completely in the wrong. In this connection the Lord says:

And when they are told, "You shall follow what God has sent down," they say, "We follow only what we found our forefathers doing." What if their forefathers lacked both knowledge and guidance?
The allegory of those who disbelieve is like those who parrot whatever they hear without any understanding. They are deaf, dumb, and blind. Thus, they fail to understand. (2:170-171)

In the preceding verses, the Lord has given a representation of the state of those who were blinded by imitation. He who calls them to righteousness is likened to one who parrots whatever he hears without any comprehension. They are deaf, dumb, blind and devoid of understanding on account of their holding fast to the practices of their forefathers and refusing to put them to the test of reason.

ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(2)

The Lord says that if those unbelievers were asked to follow what the Lord has sent down, they will say "We follow only what we found our forefathers doing," to which the Lord replies rousing the instinct of reason in them: "What if their forefathers lacked both the knowledge and the guidance?"

Then the Lord gave the above representation of them which no one with a whit of pride would tolerate, provoking them thereby to seek an outlet to their sorry state.

In order to move them from this inaction, the Lord then applies different reasoning.

And when they are told, "Come to what God has sent down; come to this Messenger," they say, "Enough for us is what we found our forefathers doing." What if their forefathers had neither knowledge, nor guidance? (5:104)

That is, if the unbelievers were called to follow the guidance of the Qur'an they say the knowledge which we inherited from our forefathers is sufficient for us to which the Lord says:

"Will you still say so if your forefathers lacked both the knowledge and the guidance?"

And in this connection the Lord demanded of the unbelievers to support their claim of the so-called knowledge of their forefathers:

Have you any certain knowledge to substantiate your claim that you may produce to us? (6:148)

In another verse the Lord says [printed as "days" in the original, apparent typo]:

Bring me a scripture before the Qur'an or some vestiges of ancient knowledge to support your claim if you are truthful. (46:4)

In describing the end of those who imitate their forefathers without any knowledge or a book to guide them, the Lord says:

M. Farid Wajdi

That is when the leaders shall disown their followers. They shall undergo the punishment and no help shall come to them. The followers shall then say, "If we only get a second chance, we shall disown them as they have disowned us." Thus, God will show them the consequences of their deeds; nothing but sorrow for them, and they shall never exit from the hellfire. (2:166,167)

And:

The Lord will say unto the unbelievers on the Judgment day: "Enter ye into Hell together with nations of jinn and of men who have preceded you;" so oft as one nation enters, it shall curse its sister, until they have all entered in succession, the last of them shall say unto the first: "O Lord, these have led us astray, deal Thou unto them a double punishment of hell-fire;" and the Lord will say: "It shall be doubled unto all, but ye know not."
And the first of them shall say unto the last: "Ye have no advantage over us and we have both been in error; taste ye therefore the punishment for that which ye have done." (7:38-39)

In the preceding verses, the Lord points out that the followers of disbelief are just as culpable as the leaders, for the Lord has endowed all men with reason and required them to distinguish between truth and falsehood. They are therefore equally responsible for their deeds and none of them has an advantage over the other. And when the imitators have asked the Lord to deal a double punishment to their leaders whose example they have imitated, the Lord has adjudged them both responsible and has doubled the punishment to them all. Such was the Lord's warning against persistence in blind imitation.

In another chapter of the Qur'an the Lord says:

ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(2)

قال ادخلوا في أمم قد خلت من قبلكم من الجن والإنس في النار كلما دخلت أمة لعنت أختها حتى إذا اداركوا فيها جميعا قالت أخراهم لأولاهم ربنا هؤلاء أضلونا فآتهم عذابا ضعفا من النار قال لكل ضعف ولكن لا تعلمون وقالت أولاهم لأخراهم فما كان لكم علينا من فضل فذوقوا العذاب بما كنتم تكسبون
قال هذا فوج مقتحم معكم لا مرحبا بهم إنهم صالوا النار قالوا بل أنتم لا مرحبا بكم أنتم قدمتموه لنا فبئس القرار

Unto the leaders it shall be said:
"This is a company which shall be plunged with you into Hell," to which they shall say: "No welcome is there for them, they shall burn in hell-fire like us." And the followers shall say unto the leaders: "But ye, too! There shall be no welcome for you. It was ye who brought us to this and wretched is the abode." (38:59-60)

On the entry of the unbelievers into Hell, angels shall say to the leaders: "This is a company of your followers that shall be plunged with you into Hell." The leaders shall say: "No welcome is there for them, they have had minds to distinguish between truth and falsehood and their punishment is hell-fire like us." The followers will retort: "No welcome for you either, you have enticed us into this delusion and wretched indeed is our ending."

The Lord (may He be praised and glorified!) has seen fit to impress on us by such variegated forms of eloquence the fact that leaders and followers will come to the one and same evil end, and it avails the latter not to be followers of others so long as they have had minds by which to distinguish between truth and falsehood.

By these solemn admonitions, Islam has demolished the principle of blind imitation of forefathers and has awakened the conciousness of individual responsibility. It has delivered the weak from their bondage to the strong and smashed down the invulnerable walls of exclusiveness which the leaders raised for their own ends.

By demolishing blind imitation Islam has aimed at abolishing a state of ignorance in which men were enslaved to certain sects that made learning and religion an exclusive right only to themselves, and arbitrarily ruled the people even as absolute masters do. They suffered no censure or criticism to be passed on their actions and declined the admission, into their exclusive body, of any outsider though he may have been a noted man of learning and genius.

Should this state of things become established in a nation, learning and religion will be rendered the exclusive right of a sect which will exploit them in their own interest and subject them to the dictates of their passion. In course of time, they will become a collection of stereotyped forms which will check the onward march of progress and stand between nations and the realization of their objectives.

Freedom from the shackles of imitation was the objective of Islam and it has led its people to a perfect state of cooperation between learning and religion as well as between sentiment and reason. Through this cooperation Muslims have attained to the height of progress which gave them the world-leadership for many a century and it is assured that they will regain that leadership once they follow faithfully, the tenets of their glorious religion.

ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(2)

GOD'S MESSAGE TO HUMANITY: THE ULTIMATE PROOF OF AUTHENTICITY*
by Yusuf Amin Wali, Ph.D.
Treasurer, Supreme Council of the Muslim Young Men's Association, Cairo, Egypt

God's finalized and completed message delivered in the Arabic language.** However, since it is intended for all the people, in all places, at all the times, it carries within its composition the proof of authenticity which can be understood and fully appreciated by anyone regardless of his tongue. On these pages, the reader is presented with physical, examinable, and indisputable evidence that the Qur'an is the unaltered message from the Almighty to His creation. Seekers of the truth shall find herein sure guidance towards their goal. The unfortunate souls who are afflicted with various prejudices shall be utterly blinded (Qur'an 18:57)

The greatest affliction of man is the lack of identity and purpose. Once a correct identity is established, and once the purpose behind our existence is defined, such affliction can, sequentially, be removed. The vast majority of people spend their lives under the pretense that the body constitutes one's identity. Thus, they spend their lives caring for the body, the mere shell of their real self; working, laboring, fighting among themselves, hating, loving, and struggling in the service of their vanishing entity. When it is too late, i.e., when they shed the shell, they discover that their real self was left unfed, undeveloped, and miserably neglected. Their eternal existence in such a feeble state can be rightly described as "hell." On the other hand, those who are fortunate enough to overcome this identity crisis will be able to define their purpose, place the emphasis during their earthly existence on the right goal, and live and act accordingly. They will realize that developing their eternal entity requires putting the body in the service of the soul, and not the other way around.

*Condensed from the book "Miracle of the Qur'an: Significance of the Mysterious Alphabets" by Rashad Khalifa, Islamic Productions International, Inc., St. Louis, Missouri, USA. 1973.
**It had to be delivered in some language. The Qur'an itself states that its language is immaterial; that the believers shall grasp the full message therein, regardless of their mother tongue; and that even the Arabic-speaking people will not understand it unless they qualify therefor by sincerity and devotion (6:25, 18:57; 4:44; 56:77-79.)

ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(2): 91-104

GOD'S MESSAGE TO HUMANITY

Our Creator has informed us of the ways and means of developing and caring for the soul. His message, the one and only message, started with the creation of Adam, the first man; the first messenger. Subsequent messengers, such as Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad (may God bestow His blessings and peace upon them), delivered the same message whereby man can feed and develop his real self. With the arrival of God's final messenger, THE MESSAGE was finalized, and the Almighty Himself vowed to preserve it for all subsequent generations, and to protect it from alteration or distortion(1). Moreover, the Almighty has vowed to embed in His message such proof of authenticity that each generation can witness; leaving no excuse for anyone to disbelieve(2). This article, which is but a glimpse from a vast computerized study of the Qur'an (3), offers an example of the visible miracles which are embedded in the Qur'an to prove its authenticity. Only those completely enslaved by worldly matters will deny the indisputable proof presented here. To appreciate this evidence which comes to all of humanity from their Creator, one needs no special knowledge of the Qur'an's language.

The Qur'anic Initials

One of the unique features of the Qur'an is the occurrence at the beginning of certain suras of alphabets which bear no apparent meanings. These alphabets, henceforth called "Qur'anic Initials," are not known in any other literary work.

Of the 114 suras in the Qur'an 28 begin with one set of Qur'anic initials, and one sura is prefixed with two sets of Qur'anic initials. Each set of Qur'anic initials consists of a number of letters ranging between one and five. The different sets of Qur'anic initials and the suras where they occur are listed in Table 1. As shown in that table, there are 14 different sets of Qur'anic initials, and the number of letters which participate in the make-up of these initials is also 14. The 14 letters involved in the formation of Qur'anic initials are Alif (A), Ha (H), Ra (R), Sin (S), Sad (S), Ta (T), 'Ayn ('A), Qaf (Q), Kaf (K), Lam (L), Mim (M), Nun (N), Ha (H), and Ya (Y). These letters are known in the Muslim literature, more specifically among the Sufi mystics, as "the illumination letters." The other half of the alphabet, the 14 letters not involved, are known as "the darkness letters."

The suras which contain Qur'anic initials are listed in their recorded sequence in Table 2.

ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(2)

This article will deal with the miraculous features embedded in only two sets of these Qur'anic initials, namely, Qaf (Q) and Ta Sin Mim (TSM). For the complete computerized study of all 14 sets of Qur'anic initials, the reader may consult reference 3 listed below.

The Qur'anic Initial Qaf (Q)

There are two suras in the Qur'an which bear this initial, namely, sura Al-Shura (number 42) and sura Qaf (number 50). Although sura Al-Shura is more than twice as long as sura Qaf, these two Qaf-initialed suras contain the same number of the letter Qaf (Q), 57. At this point, we must stop and reflect on the significance of this observation. To derive correct conclusions, the following points should be borne in mind:
1. This observation is an undeniable fact; no speculation or guesswork is involved. It is a fact that anyone, anywhere in the world, can establish for himself, regardless of his language. The only prerequisite would be familiarity with one letter of the Arabic alphabet; the letter Qaf (Q). The letter looks like this: ق. When placed at the beginning of a word, it looks like this: قـ. When placed in the middle of the word, the letter Qaf (Q) looks like this: ـقـ. At the end of a word, the letter looks like this: ـق.
With this minute amount of information, any person can look up the Qur'an, count the frequency of the letter Qaf in sura Al-Shura (No. 42) and in sura Qaf (No. 50). This person will physically establish THE FACT that the only two suras in the Qur'an which are initiated with letter Qaf contain the same number of this letter, namely 57.
2. The second fact one must bear in mind is that the Qur'an was revealed over a period of 23 years. Its verses came to us widely separated from each other both in time and place. Thus, sura Al-Shura, for example, contains 4 verses which were revealed in Medina, namely, verses 23, 24, 25, and 27. The other 49 verses were revealed, separately, in Mecca (300 miles from Medina). Sura Qaf consists of 44 Meccan verses and one Medinian verse (No. 38).
These historical facts are significant, since they point out to us that the Author of the Qur'an knew in advance the alphabetical distribution within the Qur'an. One can readily see from the revelation system that such knowledge is beyond the ability of any human or group of humans(4). The evidence is overwhelmingly presented in this minute glimpse of the total study that the Qur'an could not be man-made. To indicate this advance knowledge to the recipients of His message, the Almighty Author placed the initial Qaf (Q) at the beginning of these two suras which contain the same number of this particular letter.
